Jasmine Thompson - singing sensation

By: Diana Lucas | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We talk to tech savvy singing sensation 15 year old Jasmine Thompson

Summary:
Jasmine Thompson

Aint Nobody loves me better a 1982 hit from singer/songwriter Chaka Khan has had a reboot from an up and coming singer/songwriter forty years her junior. Jasmine Thompson is the name of this rising star and when she released the acoustic cover version of Chaka Khan’s “Aint Nobody” she was believe it or not 10 years old. The song went all the way to number 2 on the UK charts and peaked in other countries.
The video has received over 2.5 million views online.

Five years later at the ripe ‘old’ age of 15, you could call Jasmine a singing sensation. She started out putting cover versions of songs on You Tube, simply recording them herself, the hits and views grew and grew…her videos became more professional and Jasmine interaction and social media savvy’ness has seen her You Tube subscribers escalate. As of 2016, Jasmine’s YouTube channel has over 2 million subscribers and over 280 million views.

And Jasmine is now writing her own songs. In September she self-released her debut album Bundle of Tantrums which included the singles "La La La", "Let Her Go" and "Titanium".

We profile Jasmine just before her concert in South Africa ( Our television airing 17th April is the night of her concert so very timeous), and explore her road to success, her song writing, her chart topping videos and her tech savvy brand building triumph ….which started at a mere 10 years old.

Press Release:


Jasmine Thompson
When 15-year-old Jasmine Thompson released her acoustic cover version of Chaka Khan’s “Aint Nobody” at the tender age of thirteen, the song climbed the UK charts and peaked in other countries. Videos she’s posted online have since received millions of views and launched her international career on stage. Carte Blanche catches up with the tech-savvy singer on tour in South Africa.


Script:



Hi! My name is Jasmine Thompson. I am from London. I post videos of me singing here :)
Link
This how10 year old Londoner Jasmine Thompson started her singing career she was a young girl with a dream that to most would seem sheer fantasy.

Jasmine: I’ve always enjoyed music even when I was really singing really badly when I didn’t know how to sing and then what happened was my mom she knew that I loved music and she helped me post on You Tube.

Link
Alone in her bedroom, or sometimes with the help of her mother, Jasmine started putting cover versions of
songs she liked on YouTube. She
would blog a description of how she felt, sometimes apologizing
for the poor technical quality and promising to do better next
time.

Jasmine: Our YouTube videos were very relaxed and homely but the process of making them took ages we didn’t know what we were doing the very first video was my mom crouched lying down in the corner of my Mom’s bedroom on this tiny ipod, because we have a very small house, almost a flat and we would use as much space as possible pushing back the furniture to one side of the room just so we could get the perfect angle the perfect lighting when I look back my videos were really hilarious.

V/O
When Jasmine’s was 8 her mother helped her daughter develop with piano and singing lessons.

Jasmine: That’s why I really loved my mom about this she was really supportive studying recordings we used to use Q base she bought this manual and read this whole thing and tried to make my covers as professional as we could… music is my way of therapy it’s the only way I can properly give across my emotions so my mom saw that and she helped me.
Derek: She didn’t say Jasmine get in your bedroom and record a cover
Jasmine No she didn’t say that.
Derek: Your cat also fancied some stardom when you were recording the Lady Gaga cover.
Jasmine: She was lying there and she had this sudden idea to roll around on the bed and spaz out, but she was really funny.

Link
…..In a matter of years Jasmine had become an internet sensation her YouTube channel grew to more than 2 million subscribers and this cover of Let Her Go by Passenger has had more than 28 million views.
Jasmine: I don’t know why it went so well I think I was really moody that day, I was trying so many different takes and it was just not working and I was ok lets just try it and I was mom get out, and I was really moody, I kicked her out, I did it by myself because I was really moody and then it worked.
Ravi Naidooi: Well I think what she has probably done is broken all the traditional barriers for musicians. Before a musician would have to do a demo go to a record company and then hope that somebody would sign up now it’s different. You do the demo you put it up on You Tube, sound cloud you get hits and then the record companies are calling you to go can we sign you?
Derek: Is your success a case of really tech savvy brand building or has there been luck involved?
Jasmine I think a lot of luck, but also being careful of what I post I was also very lucky because I was in a very positive environment when I was on YouTube I had haters, I also had a lot of supporters who kinda kept me going. Ever since I started You tube I always been on Twitter at least for an hour a day trying to communicate with my followers because some of them have been following me since I started You Tube, they are so sweet they are like my second family.
Link
When Jasmine posted a cover of Chaka Khan’s Ain’t Nobody it got a fair response then it became part of a Sainsbury’s advert and finally it was remixed by German DJ Felix Jaen. It became her biggest hit and the name of Jasmine Thompson was firmly engraved on the music world.

V/O
This cover has received over 230 million views an incredible feat for any artist

Link
When YouTube launched more than a decade ago nobody thought you could actually make out of it. There was no branding it was literally a playground for weird and wonderful ideas but You Tube and streaming have grown and now the stars make more from the digital platform than physical sales.
Ravi: You remember the days when everybody used to send around cat videos on you tube right now it’s a platform you can now create You Tube music playlists with all the videos out so actually the desired platform for most musicians is now put it on You Tube or create a You Tube channel that just gathers all the content so it’s music, its their content it could be performances that they do so the delivery mechanisms of artists getting out there now is far greater than the traditional music platforms.
Derek: The digital platform for music is now bigger than physical sales.
Ravi: You have to use New York as an example there is not a physical CD store that is available right, we run our chart show on line 947 and KFM all on music sales, on digital downloads so CD sales as in physical CD sales is probably going to beDigital platform obsolete in the next 5 years.
V/O
And in September 2013 Jasmine self released her debut album Bundle of Tantrums.
Jasmine: I was in school and my friends were likeOMG you are releasing an album, what does this mean? I was like I don’t know all I am doing is releasing something on to a platform and people might buy it.
Derek You release bundle of Tantrums, your twitter handle is Tantrum Jazz are we saying something here, where you a tantrum child?
Jasmine: Okay, there is a story so I don’t really get on with my stepdad that much so they decided to call me Tantrum Jazz because I was always having tantrums with him, but I was a really nice child.
Derek: And these days?
Jasmine: These days No I get on with him really well.

V/O
Jasmine signed up with Warner Music in 2014 ….she’s doing live concerts all over the world- this weekend in South Africa
Jasmine: The first time I ever did a live show it was the complete opposite of doing a video It was crazy I walked on stage and it was like a …room full of 1500 people all staring at me, singing my song people were actually nodding along and they were having fun and the next day I went back to school and I was in a maths class and I was like OMG I am in a maths class right now last night I was in front of crowds singing my song showing them who I wanted to be.
V/O
And then there’s the question that every parent is going to ask what happened to studies and homework when Jasmine became known for her singing talents before even going to High School.
Jasmine: Last year I left school to do home school because that’s when I realised music was 100% the only thing I wanted to do and I had the opportunity to go and travel the world but still also do my schoolwork. So I have tutors when I am on the road and I am also learning so much, just by going and talking to all the people I meet while on tour.
V/O
Newly released is Adore, a song written by Jasmine and writing her own songs is the direction she wants to go
….For Jasmine Thompson at only 15 years old the future looks bright.
Derek: Jasmine do you ever pinch your self and say cant believe what’s happened in five short years?
Jasmine: That happened really recently I was in the studio and I basically broke down crying from happiness…it was a surreal moment and it just hit me. It was like that moment that people say before you die that your life is going to flash before your eyes that was a bit like then because I kinda saw l imagined being back in my mom’s room filming the lazy song and then just like all of a sudden five years later I have never felt so happy in my life so that was very recently.
